#4199. Nioh 3 patch finally makes summons useful in boss fights, brings free armour for everyone

There's a new Nioh 3 patch out in the wild, and it's one that any player who regularly summons in boss fights will really appreciate.

Team Ninja continues to work on Nioh 3. The developer has been releasing regular updates for the action RPG since its launch in early February. Earlier patches have addressed major bugs like healing item use inconsistencies, and more have arrived since to tackle various balance and loot-related issues.

Today’s patch, version 1.04, is a major one, coming in at well over 1GB. There’s plenty here worth getting excited about, so let’s dig in.

To begin with, this is the patch that adds the promised free armour sets for both Ninja, and Samurai. When Nioh 3 reached one million sales, Team Ninja said it would gift every player the Thunderous set in celebration, and the set’s two variants are now available in-game.

The more interesting side of the patch is, unsurprisingly, its change log. There appears to be a focus on online co-op and AI summons in this one, with various tweaks to the make the process more rewarding, and, in some cases, worthwhile.

The amount of Glory obtained when you complete a mission in multiplayer has been increased, regardless of which player was the host. The other major change mainly affects AI Benevolent Grave summons, making it so bosses will no longer target a single player for almost the entirety of the fight.

While summoning AI helpers has always been useful in Nioh 3, they didn’t always help in boss fights, specifically because the boss tended to focus on the player who summoned them, leaving the AI to run around eating AoE hits before dying.

Patch 1.04 makes a couple of welcome gameplay tweaks to the feel of combat. Ninjutsu, and Onmyo Magic will now hit their targets more consistently in situations where there’s a difference in elevation between the player and the enemy.

In the same vein, you’ll now be able to attack (quick/strong) right after jumping, which removes the pause that previously buffered the attack instead. This could mean even more air combos that don’t specifically require Martial Arts.

You can look forward to a couple of quality of life tweaks in this patch, too, such as the change that allows the game to automatically send any Sudama Soul Cores dropped by merchants to your item box. This happens from the second one onwards, which means you won’t have to pick half a dozen each time you go to sell a batch of items.

Speaking of the item box, the limit of forging materials has been increased for some of them. If you’ve been running Battle Scroll missions and Expeditions for gear, you’ll be happy to know that you can now exit the session from the main menu directly.

There’s plenty more to patch 1.04, including fixes and balance tweaks for several weapons, such as Samurai dual swords, odachi, and more for a few Ninja weapons, too. The patch also brings several bug fixes to the game.

You can read the full set of patch notes on Steam.

#4198. Countdown: Zelda: Ocarina Of Time Dungeon Crawl #7 - Grave Expectations

Would you look at that, we are rapidly closing in on the release date of Ocarina of Time on Switch 2 and the end of my Dungeon Crawl replay of the N64 original. Doesn't time fly?

With the much-discussed Water Temple out of the way, it was my decision where to head next. Despite Saria telling me to head to the desert, I am dead set in my ways, so, as I do on every replay, it was back to Kakariko Village to see what was going on in the graveyard.

I'm sure you all know by now, but I'm going to be discussing temple spoilers here, so if you are still saving yourself for the Switch 2 remake, you might want to turn back now.

I can't remember why I initially chose to head to the Shadow Temple first, over its sandy companion, but I can never bring myself to break the order that I have relied on for the last ~25 years. And so, after polishing off the Bottom of the Well (still nightmare fuel in 2026), it was time to play the Nocturne of Shadow and pass through its torch-filled entrance.

I have a strange relationship with the Shadow Temple. I like its ideas, but I find it a little linear and repetitive — particularly after the exploration-encouragement of the temples that precede it. I've never really managed to put my finger on why this is, but playing through it again this time, it hit me: you get all the tools to solve every puzzle too quickly.

This is a dungeon that relies on two items: the Lens of Truth (obtained from the Bottom of the Well before you've even set foot in the Temple) and the Hover Boots (found very early on after solving the dungeon's introductory skull puzzle). With both of these in hand, you have everything you need to beat the whole damn thing. Maybe it's the multiple playthroughs in me talking, but... doesn't this mean you've already solved all the puzzles before you get to them?

I love the Lens of Truth; it blew me away when I first played it, and I still get a kick out of it today, moving the camera incrementally to see if a wall is real or not, but let's not pretend that it has all that much depth to it. It shows you things that aren't there. That's it. This means there are very few ways that the Shadow Temple can develop puzzles around it. If you walk into a room and the solution isn't immediately obvious, popping the lens on will likely reveal the answer.

We see it in the first puzzle with the one 'true' skull. In the room with the hidden 'Stone Umbrella' block to stop the spike pistons. Even in the central, guillotine-filled room with its invisible platforms. Magic vials are so common in this dungeon that you can keep it equipped for pretty much your whole run and play each room as a simple walk from A to B.

The Hover Boots are more of the same: see a gap you can't cross and the Lens of Truth didn't reveal a hidden platform? Just hover over it.

Unlike in other dungeons, where some of these puzzles would have been revealed before you had the tools to complete them, there's very little mental note-taking required in this one, which makes the whole thing feel a little breezy.

That said, for all of its linearity, I can't in good faith knock it too much, because the vibes are immaculate. I'll give it to Bongo Bongo, that guy knows how to put together gothic architecture.

The whole place is so damn macabre! Skulls on the walls, spinning grim reapers wielding scythes, closing-in walls like a Death Star trash compactor. This boss knows how to work an aesthetic! Compared to some of the previous dungeon's drier visuals, this one has such a firm identity that there's no chance of getting lost.

After making my way through the motions and boarding the boat of death, I bombed the river-crossing pillar (it still feels good) and headed to the boss room.

I'm going to stay positive as I wrap things up, because I really like Bongo Bongo. There's an argument to be made that the constant drumming (and subsequent bouncing) makes this petty percussionist one of the more frustrating bosses in the game, and in fairness... that's probably right. But! You put the lack of solid ground aside for a second and you've got a battle all about timing, dodging, and magic management. I wouldn't describe it as Dark Souls-like, but it is ace!

The 'shoot the two giant hands' Zelda boss trope is tried and tested these days, but this is absolutely one of the best of them — particularly when you start seeing it as a perilous game of Rock, Paper, Scissors.

Without some rather substantial changes to the item placement, I can't see the Shadow Temple ever being one of my favourites. It's a little too linear and simple for my pro-Water-Temple heart, I'm afraid. But (as I've said before in this series), even the drier Zelda dungeons are still a damn good time!

Truthfully, I can't wait to see how the dark aesthetic and big boss turn out in the remake.

I'm approaching the finish line next week, as I tackle the game's last 'main' dungeon — don't worry, I'll be doing a special finale, too. So, don your desert boots and sand goggles, and I'll catch you all in the next one.

#4197. The Sims 4 patch makes it so your public lot gatherings won't be interrupted by rogue Sims

Stranger Sims will no longer just crash your public lot events in The Sims 4 to talk about whatever.

The Sims 4 will soon get a new update to resolve a number of issues, some of which have long caused headaches for players. The latest update will arrive March 17 on PC and Mac, followed by PlayStation and Xbox at an unspecified time later.

Outside of the fixes themselves, the patch also makes good on the recent re-commitment to continue improving quality of life for players, so there’s plenty here longtime players will appreciate.

In the latest episode of The Sims 4’s Laundry List blog series, where the developer goes through the most reported problems with the game and how it plans to solve them, we got a rundown of what to expect from next week’s patch.

You can look forward to five major fixes in this one, but arguably the most important is a change to how Sims determine who they speak with on a lot. This is especially relevant for public lots, where Sims would sometimes interrupt ongoing conversations by barging in and starting a conversation with your Sim.

Going forward, Sims will prioritise familiar Sims with whom they already have rapport, and be less likely to latch onto strangers. If you’ve witnessed a date your Sim was on get interrupted because of that, you’ll certainly appreciate the change.

Speaking of budding romance, Prom is coming back to in-game Calendars, and Sims can once again attend. Maxis said this will work with new and existing saves, and that you should also expect Prom goals to be completable once again.

Pets and animals get some love in this patch, too. First, pets and horses will no longer get lost in Premade Households. The fix prevents that from happening in new saves, but if you already had that happen to you in your current save, it’ll still be there.

You may now also assign animals to an Animal Shed after moving your house to a new lot, so you hopefully won’t be confused as to why they’re stuck in your inventory. This fix applies to existing saves as well as new ones.

Lower down the list of urgent fixes is an update that makes it so Sims’ eye blinking will show fully closed eyes for most interactions. The upcoming patch also comes with a host of Sims autonomy fixes, including one that prevents them from excessively flirting with each other.

Catch up on the full list at the link near the top of the page. And, in case you missed it, Maxis recently announced that The Sims 4 will soon get paid mods, something that many in the community are skeptical about.

#4196. Cozy Magical Sim Witchbrook Gets A January Release Date

Witchbrook is a game I've been looking forward to for a while, and today's Nintendo Indie World showcase finally confirmed the game's release date: January 28. Any game from Chucklefish, best known for publishing Stardew Valley and developing the Wargroove series, is worthy of my attention, and Witchbrook looks more exciting the more we see of it. The game mixes cute pixel art with a robust suite of magical gameplay systems. As you go to a witch college to learn spells, you'll also build a life in the town, making friends, working jobs, decorating your home, and more. It was an appealing pitch when it was announced nearly 10 years ago in 2017, and it remains so to this day. Witchbrook's release date was announced during today's Nintendo-specific stream, but it's coming to all major platforms: PS5, Xbox Series X/S, Switch 2, Switch, and PC.

#4194. Crimson Desert PC specs don't keep resolution and framerate targets a secret, and they don't use upscaling for everything either

Finally, a PC specification list that actually indicates resolution and framerate targets, and doesn't leave console players behind.

Crimson Desert is a little over one week away from release, and developer Pearl Abyss has delivered the official, final list of specs for the game. The twist is that the specs not only include useful information for PC players, they also cover similarly relevant details for console players, who traditionally don’t get mentioned in those reveals.

The specs are decently detailed, but more surprisingly - except for a single instance - they don’t include upscaling on PC, another thing games have gotten too comfortable using, even with their lowest specs.

On the official Crimson Desert website, developer Pearl Abyss has delivered a chunky post breaking down five different sets of PC requirements for the upcoming open-world action RPG. Each set indicates the graphics preset being used - and crucially, the resolution and framerate targets you can expect with each.

With the exception of the Minimum spec, all other presets do not appear to rely on upscaling of any kind. They do not say, however, whether ray tracing is being used with any of them, which is a feature that will throw all of those specs out of whack.

That same transparency also extends to non-PC platforms, which traditionally get few, if any, details about their own resolution and framerate targets. The console set of specs are extensive, just like PC, covering both PlayStation, and Xbox.

It’s granular enough to indicate which upscaling tech is being used, where applicable. This is relevant for owners of a PS5 Pro, a console that has access to Sony’s PSSR upscaling, alongside the standard AMD FSR tech the base console - and Xbox - use.

The developer has also revealed the base resolution for each mode across each console, and the resolution the image will be upscaled to using whichever tech is being utilised.

And, if you’re one of the five people who play games on Mac, you’ll be thrilled to know that the specs also include a section for Mac devices, split between the different Mac chips. The quality preset being used with each is not clear, however.

Finally, there's a set of specs for the Rog Xbox Ally, covering both the X and S models.

Crimson Desert arrives March 20 on PC, PS5, and Xbox Series X/S. You can expect more coverage from us at release and beyond.

#4193. Nintendo Indie World Showcase Recap: Everything We Saw

The year is nearing its conclusion, and the last big AAA titles are rolling out one-by-one. But today, it was all about the independent titles on Nintendo's latest Indie World Showcase, highlighting new games from smaller indie teams coming to the Switch and Switch 2.

Here's everything we saw at the October 2026 Nintendo Indie World Showcase.

Today's Indie World Showcase started with a big headliner, as the long-awaited witch-life simulator Witchbrook got a release date. Chucklefish and Robtality's cozy magical world goes live on January 28, 2027.

Fans of 3D platformers should probably keep an eye on Winds of Viridia, which looks like a colorful game with a lot of interesting movement and exploration. Shark Jump's fantastical platformer is arriving next year, but if the wait's too long, a free demo is coming today on the eShop.

From one of the co-creators of Celeste, City of None has a gorgeous pixelated art style and colors that immediately remind me of Game Boy Color classics. It's a 2D platformer where you leap around, fight enemies, and explore the strange city around you. The jumping and fighting look solid, and I really like the mysterious atmosphere and art direction. City of None's set for sometime in 2027.

The sword-surfing adventure from the makers of Abzu and Journey is coming to Nintendo Switch 2 on October 29, 2026 - tomorrow! It's a gorgeous adventure that earned a Must-Play badge from us, so it's worth your time if you like the kinds of gorgeous, beautiful adventures Giant Squid (developer of Abzu) is known for.

Take an overhead camera angle, brawler gameplay, and some John Wick sensibilities, and you've got Tenjutsu, a stylish roguelike where you use your martial arts prowess to tear apart crime syndicates. I really enjoy the look and vibe of this one, and it's from one of the designers of Dead Cells, too. Tenjutsu might be one to keep an eye on when it arrives on Switch 2 in 2027.

RPG fans have been eating well, and it looks like the feast could continue next year with Threads of Time. The time-traveling RPG is coming to both Switch and Switch 2 next summer, and it's looking absolutely gorgeous.

Ah, raccoons. Nature's most adorable little scamps. If you and your friends have ever wanted to live out the dream of being a rambunctious band of raccoons wreaking havoc on the town, Dumpster Gang sets out to give you just that fantasy in March 2027.

I've already enjoyed quite a bit of Super Battle Golf on PC, so I'll tell you now: if you enjoy golf games and want some Mario Party annoy-your-friends antics wound around them, Super Battle Golf should be on your radar for its March 25, 2027 launch on Switch 2.

Another port of a PC multiplayer mainstay, the co-op physics-driven horror-looter R.E.P.O. is coming to Switch 2 in 2027. This is one for the crowd that likes to be scared one moment and laughing hysterically the next.

Rounding out the co-op section, Haunted Paws has you and a pal playing as a pair of pups searching for their person in a haunted mansion. The side-scrolling 3D look makes it seem like a less-scary Little Nightmares, and the concept is pretty fun. Look for this one on Switch and Switch 2 in May 2027, or try out the free demo later today.

Enjoy shrines, towns, and strange night-time journeys into the unknown? Follow a fox girl and her frog friend on an adventure through a strange island in Kitsune: The Journey of Adashino on Switch 2 and Switch in spring 2027. I've said it a few times in this recap, but wow, the art here is great.

The second entry in the slime-collecting, home-building sim adventure is coming to Switch 2. Pick up adorable slimes with your vacuum, build a home for them, and explore the Rainbow Island around you in January 2027. Plus, there's an exclusive in-game item for the Switch 2 version.

From the makers of Cozy Grove, this multiplayer game encourages players to build a home above the clouds with friends and explore the world around them. Spirit Crossing looks like a big world to make your own alongside your pals, starting November 16, 2026 on both Switch and Switch 2.

Want something a little sillier? My Arms Are Longer Now is a game about, well, really long arms. With numerous Australian comedians lending their vocal talents to the project, this seems like it could be a quirky, charming, and delightfully funny experience when it arrives on both Switch and Switch 2 on March 11, 2027.

The delightfully Game Boy-styled critter delivery game Petal Runner is aiming for a full launch. I've played a bit of this one at events over the years, and it's charmed me every time. If you like nostalgic adventures with a surprisingly heartfelt core, you should mark down the March 8, 2027 launch, or check out the free demo arriving later today.

The chaotic coin-pushing game Raccoin is coming to Nintendo Switch 2. It's just like those token-shoving games you remember from arcades but with a number of wild and wacky means of pushing even more coins over the edge run-over-run. Raccoin: Chaos Max Edition hits Switch 2 on November 10, 2026, and a free demo is out later today.

#4192. Round Up: Pikmin Day 2026 - Updates, Demo And New Animated Shorts

Nintendo surprised us with a Pikmin-themed Direct this weekend, announcing Pikmin Day! If you haven't already watched the video, here's everything from the broadcast:

On this page: Round Up: Pikmin Day 2026 - Updates, Demo And New Animated Shorts

Joining MAR10 Day and other events such as Pokémon Day, is Pikmin Day! This will be an annual event every year on 1st November. Miyamoto explained how this came about:

Shigeru Miyamoto: "We're going to start calling November 1st, Pikmin Day. In the first Pikmin game, released on Nintendo GameCube in 2001, the red, blue and yellow Pikmin made their debut. If you imagine those three Pikmin as the number one, that makes November 1st, Pikmin Day!"

A free demo of Pikmin 4 - Nintendo Switch 2 Edition + Dandori Academy is out 2nd November 2026. It will include the game's opening area Sun-speckled Terrace, along with two stages of Dandori Academy. Save data will also transfer over to the full game.

Nintendo also provided a quick rundown about the features coming in the Switch 2 Edition of Pikmin 4.

This includes voice commands for Oatchi with the built-in system mic. And then there's the new mode, Dandori Academy, where you'll take on challenges, collect the treasure, and take an exam. You'll receive medals based on your performance.

News Pikmin 4 Finally Gets The 'Switch 2 Edition' It Deserves This November

Before you can venture in you'll need a Cave Map, attached to postcards. When you've got your map, you can then send out Pikmin to explore the cave and battle creatures. Win the battle and you'll get all sorts of treasures.

Additionally, there'll be in-app cave maps you can unlock by taking exams in Pikmin 4 Nintendo Switch 2 Edition + Dandori Academy:

Review Pikmin Bloom - Pokémon GO's Sister Title Is A Glorious, Glorified Pedometer

Following on from past animated Pikmin shorts, Nintendo Pictures and Miyamoto have unveiled the latest series, 'Hello! Pikmin'.

The first short aired during the Nintendo Direct and the rest will be released on the Nintendo Today! app and other Nintendo channels. Two more episodes are out this month, and from December onwards, one video will be released per month.

Nintendo has also announced it's hosting a Treehouse event today where it will showcase Pikmin 4 Nintendo Switch 2 Edition + Dandori Academy. You'll be able to watch it on the official Nintendo YouTube channel.

A special broadcast timed in with Pikmin Day

As part of the Pikmin Day celebrations, the following icons are now available:

"Redeem your #MyNintendo Platinum Points to collect custom icons from Pikmin, available until Nov 28 at 5pm PT on Nintendo Switch 2 and Nintendo Switch. Icon elements will be refreshed each week."

And that's a wrap on Pikmin Day for 2026!

Once again, Pikmin 4 Nintendo Switch 2 Edition + Dandori Academy arrives this month on 12th November 2026, and the demo for this version is out tomorrow.

#4191. Phantom Blade Zero: Here's How To Get The Perfect Ending, Which Is The Only Satisfying One

Phantom Blade Zero is a sprawling Wuxia adventure, the best action game of the year, and one of my favorite action games ever. It offers a lot to do, from main story quests to dozens of side quests, collectibles, hidden bosses, secret areas, and more. I highly recommend checking out Game Informer's list of Phantom Blade Zero tips and tricks before jumping in. It mentions some tasks required to achieve the perfect ending, but here I'll break down exactly what you need to see it.

As a note, getting the perfect ending in Phantom Blade Zero isn't that unreasonable. It requires doing a lot of the game's side content, but it's not shrouded in mystery or puzzles; you just need to complete certain things before heading into the finale. I'm going to keep these requirements relatively spoiler-free, and honestly, without the wider story context, they'll be a lot of mumbo jumbo proper nouns that don't really mean anything. If you're set on getting the perfect ending, I'd bookmark this page, and as you play Phantom Blade Zero, more and more of these requirements will start to make sense. However, if you think even a name or proper noun is a spoiler, be careful reading these requirements.

The following requirements don't necessarily have a set order. You could technically ignore all of this and then go after everything right before the game's "last chance to get things done" warning near the finale. So don't sweat about picking up this or that at a certain time in your journey – do it when you want to. Just make sure you have the following requirements completed before heading past the "last chance" warning.

For more, read Game Informer's Phantom Blade Zero tips and tricks, and then read Game Informer's Phantom Blade Zero review.

#4190. A puzzle game where you must avoid doing the most awkward of things: facing someone while riding an elevator

You know when you follow someone into the elevator and when they turn around to face the doors, you choose to stand still and instead meet their eyes? No, of course you don't. Everyone knows that when you're in a lift you don't under any circumstances face other people in the lift unless you know them and you're already in a conversation. Just yesterday I got into the lift with someone I sit one desk over from in the office. I dutifully looked at my phone the entire time until we were safely out of the building. Well, in the puzzle game How To Ride Elevators Like A Human you play a helpful alien who saves people who have accidentally ended up in the dreadful situation of facing one another.

Each short puzzle takes place in a compact lift where one (or several) humans are starting at each other. Using your small UFO's tractor beam, you must pick up and relocate the passengers until no one is making eyes at anyone else. You may well recognise this as a sokoban-style puzzle game, but, despite retreading familiar ground, I'm a big fan of this extraterrestrial framing. Even if I have an ulterior motive for sharing this game...

Puzzles quickly become more complicated with elevators holding increasingly more passengers, spaces in the lift being taken up by immovable heavy luggage bags, and short children introducing a challenge of two levels of eyelines. (Adults can see over them, but they can look up at adults. It's best to make them stare at some luggage.)

How To Ride Elevators Like A Human is a little janky and it shouldn't take you long to race through the ten levels in its Steam demo, but I'll admit, the main reason I'm writing about How To Ride Elevators Like A Human is because of a cruel joke I made in our work chat this morning.

Mark had shared the Forbes profile of Asha Sharma, which included the line "Unafraid to create tensions, the jacket- and sneaker-loving executive has come in clear-eyed and with swagger, indirectly questioning her predecessor’s strategy, and has shown a remarkable knack for marketing that plan with deftly written employee memos, new slogans, and strategic posts on social media, where meme after meme of Sharma also appear." (This is in addition to the detail she's planning three more waves of layoffs between now and January.) I said "People who are 'Unafraid to create tensions' are the sorts of people who get into an elevator last and don't turn to face the doors. They meet eyes with everyone they can, like the monsters they are."

So, when by chance I stumbled across a puzzle game that was essentially an Asha Sharma simulator I had to share it.

You know what the next worst thing is that someone "unafraid to create tensions" can do? Stand one step behind you on the escalator, instead of the statutory two. You're standing too close to me, Sharma, back up.

#4187. Battlefield 6 is getting a free trial next week with a decent selection of maps and modes

Battlefield 6's second-ever free trial, and the first in 2026, is upon us.

Battlefield Studios has announced that Battlefield 6 is going free to play for one week next week. Well, a portion of the game is, anyway, as part of a free trial that will include some of the game’s most popular modes and maps.

Though it does not encompass the entirety of the game, the free trial is fairly generous. Here’s what to expect.

For starters, the trial kicks off Tuesday, March 17 and will run until the following Tuesday, March 24. The trial will be accessible from Battlefield Redsec, the already free-to-play portion of the game.

Once downloaded, you’ll find a new Battlefield 6 Free Trial section in the main menu. Because Redsec and Battlefield 6 multiplayer share progression, if you played the former at any point, you’ll be able to pick up from where you left off.

The same is also true the other way around; if this is your first time with Battlefield 6, all your unlocks will carry over to the full version, as well as to Redsec if you decide stick with the free-to-play off-shoot.

Once it kicks off, you’ll find three playlists to choose from. Casual Breakthrough, All-out Warfare, and a third playlist showcasing the new Nightfall game mode and its associated map.

All-out Warfare is what you come to Battlefield for, and that playlist features Conquest, Breakthrough, as well as BF6’s newcomer Escalation - all large-scale, combined arms game modes. They will be playable across four maps. You get to play on two from Season 2: Contaminated, and Hagental Base, one from Season 1: Eastwood, and Mirak Valley from the base game.

Casual Breakthrough is based on a playlist that already exists in the core game, and it’s really designed as a nice on-ramp for new players. It also offers less intense gameplay, perfect for people grinding unlocks.

Casual Breakthrough is limited to just 16 real players (eight per team), with the rest filled up with bots. You earn the same amount of XP in those matches, except when you interact with bots, so killing a bot will net less than a human player. Outside of that, unlocks, Challenges and all other things that don’t depend on stat-tracking can be done within.

In the trial, the Casual Breakthrough playlist includes Hagental Base, Contaminated, and Eastwood.

The most interesting is the third playlist, in part because its content will also be available to owners of the full game for the first time right alongside free-to-play players. Nightfall is a playlist exclusive to the Hagental Base map.

This is a very small map, so the mode selection here is Team Deathmatch, Squad Deathmatch, and Domination. Under Nightfall conditions, lights across the entire map are turned off, so you’re going to have use your NVGs to be able to see. This is also a god opportunity to try out weapon attachments that specifically work under low-light conditions, which typically don’t get much use in multiplayer.

March 17 also marks the launch of the second stage of Battlefield 6’s Season 2, which comes with the aforementioned Nightfall content, as well as a big new update - so the timing works out nicely for everyone.

#4185. Cyberpunk 2077's Edgerunners 2 update adds two new quests, handgun dual wielding and the ability to pimp your mantis blades

A beefy new Cyberpunk 2077 update arrives tomorrow, October 22nd, fresh on the heels of the second series of the Cyberpunk Edgerunners anime which dropped earlier this week. It's dubbed update 2.5 and delivers an Edgerunners 2-themed quest alongside a heap of other additions.

As outlined in the patch's notes, CD Projekt Red and co-devs Virtuos simply aren't capable of delivering a Cyberpunk update that only adds a couple of little things. They either go hard or they go home, so there's a full-blown Edgerunners 2 prequel quest called Clampdown that offers gear from the anime, plus a new radio station featuring tracks from both Edgerunners 1 and 2.

There's also a new quest not linked specifically to the anime. Dubbed Welcome to Paradise, it has you run around learning about Night City's past and lore via projected lectures from the metropolis' founder Richard Night, with some sort of mystery in need of solving along the way. Honestly, as someone who loves just going for a wander or drive around the place when I hop into Cyberpunk, that might be the bit of this patch I'm most excited about.

That's far from it. Taking a new perk called Double Trouble will allow you to dual wield pistols and revolvers. It's a feature that's limited to power handguns, so there'll be no equipping twin katanas or finding a way to graft two assault rifles to your arms. That'd have been a bit too overpowered to live in the game without a tonne of effort on the devs' part to somehow balance the double damage it'd offer, according to CD Projekt Red's Paweł Sasko.

Another addition's something you'll be able to make use of regardless of which weapons you specialise in, assuming you're not a plain jane with no tech jammed into your skin. Hand cyberware can now be visually customised at five new vendors called glamdocs. From the looks of it, they're ripperdocs who specialise in making the likes of gorilla arms and projectile launchers look funky rather than installing the baseline version of the tech. So, you'll still need to visit ripperdocs as usual, with the glamdocs just offering a total of 40 alternative looks for cyberware that allow it to resemble the variants worn by folks from various corps and gangs across Night City. There's also some colour customisation to further the personal flavour you can add to, say, a pair of Arasaka-themed manis blades.

Cross-platform modding support is also arriving, which is bigger news for console players than it is us PC folks, though it'll make it easier to mod up the game if you're not down for hours of scrolling through the Nexus.

That's not every last thing included in the update, so make sure to check out the full notes of you're keen to be abreast of everything arriving when it drops tomorrow. Will this actually end up being the final update for game CD Projekt Red have given the appearance of trying to wean themselves off adding to for years at this point? Probably not. I'm certainly not complaining.

#4184. 'We Did This To Support The BDS Boycott' - Two Xbox Games Delisted As Celeste Developer Issues Statement

Two more games join Big Walk in the boycott movement

You may have already heard that Celeste, one of the most iconic platformers on the market, has been pulled from the Xbox Store today. It was later spotted that TowerFall, another game by the same developer, has been removed too.

Both games are still available on PlayStation, Nintendo, and PC storefronts, and the reason for their delisting on Xbox specifically has now been revealed.

In a short post from Celeste co-creator Maddy Thorson, it's explained that stopping the purchase of their games via the Xbox Store is because Microsoft is on a boycott list provided by Palestinian-led movement BDS, which wishes to boycott and divest from Microsoft-owned businesses like Xbox.

For those who’re asking, yes we delisted Celeste and TowerFall on XBox. We did this to support the BDS boycott

"For those who're asking, yes we delisted Celeste and TowerFall on XBox. We did this to support the BDS boycott"

It doesn't appear to be a hard delisting for Celeste or Towerfall, which means if you own either of the games, they should still appear in your library. Celeste was included in the Games with Gold programme way back when, and is still regarded as one of the best platformers in gaming.

BDS was also the movement credited as to why Big Walk never launched on Xbox hardware. In a statement from House House, they stated "We would love for people to be able to play the game on Xbox, but not until Microsoft and/or Xbox have been removed as BDS boycott targets".

Smith replaces former voice actor Jay Maksenuk, who can still be heard voicing Soul in various trailers and gameplay videos.

You can hear Smith's rendition of Soul in the official launch trailer for Phantom Blade Zero, however, below:

Game Informer has reached out to S-Game for a comment or statement on why the VO was changed and will update this story if it learns more.

I can pull back the curtains a bit on how last-minute this change seemingly was for Phantom Blade Zero. For most of my time playing Phantom Blade Zero for review (you can read it here), Soul was still voiced by Maksenuk. I wasn't the biggest fan of the English VO at the time, so I played most of the game using its excellent Chinese VO. However, about a week into the review period for Phantom Blade Zero, developer S-Game told me the VO for Soul had been updated (the team had previously said this update would happen ahead of time).

S-Game didn't say why or who at the time, but after listening to it post-update, it was clear to me it was Smith; his voice is iconic and hard to miss. I was basically at the end of the game at that point, so I didn't get to hear too much, but overall, I like Smith's inclusion as Soul's VO.

Nonetheless, if you're jumping into Phantom Blade Zero at launch, the Soul you play as will be voiced entirely by Smith. Let us know in the comments what you think of it after you've had some time with it!

#4182. EA is shutting down RPG veteran Bioware "to align talent and investments where we see the greatest opportunities for players and long-term growth"

Venerable RPG studio Bioware announced on it is shutting down after more than 30 years of making RPGs. The studio is responsible for making the original Baldur's Gate, Neverwinter Nights, Star Wars: Knights of the Old Republic, Dragon Age, Mass Effect, and Anthem.

As part of the announcement Bioware also say that "development on the next Mass Effect project is ending."

The post gives no reasoning for the shut down, nor does it mention its parent company EA who made the decision. In an open letter from EA's Chief Operating Officer David Tinson and Chief Studios Officer Cam Weber explained the closure, saying "we’re making deliberate choices to align talent and investments where we see the greatest opportunities for players and long-term growth."

They also cancelled a project in The Sims series code-named project Lotus, prioritising instead another called Project Evergreen.

The letter also revealed that there will be continued investment in EA's sports games, Apex Legends, Battlefield, and the next Star Wars Jedi game. Apparently, Dice and Respawn are collaborating on a new game which is likely a new Star Wars: Battlefront game.

Bloomberg reports that across EA there will be 400 layoffs, 50 of them taking place at Bioware.

Just last week, I ran a piece from Mark Darrah, a Bioware alum who had been with the studio since its Baldur's Gate days, only leaving after shipping Anthem in 2021. He explained how dangerous it was for a studio to make the scale of games Bioware was making with Mass Effect Andromeda, Anthem, and Dragon Age: Veilguard. The cost of the projects, the length of time they took to produce, and the risk they run of not selling enough companies puts the studio in "a really dangerous place". He said of his old studio that "BioWare sat right at the point where it doesn't quite work." For instance, shortly after Dragon Age: Veilguard's launch, EA CEO Andrew Wilson said the RPG had significantly underperformed, reaching only 1.5m players, less than the 3m the company had planned for.

It's also hard not to view the news in light of EA's buyout in August this year. Saudi Arabia's Public Investment Fund, equity firm Silver Lake, and Jared Kushner's Affinity partners completed their $55 billion leveraged buyout of EA, a move that both took the publisher private and added a vast amount of debt to the company's books. A year before the deal went through, unionised workers warned this buyout would mean layoffs. And, while there was an initial round in June, ahead of the deal going through, it appears this larger round is EA's first attempt to address the pressing debt they're now saddled with.

While there's no mention in EA's letter of further layoffs to come, they don't rule it out either.

#4181. Honkai: Star Rail Version 4.1 livestream reveals a pared-back, four-week update as HoYo plays catch-up

Honkai: Star Rail will continue the Planarcadia story arc in Version 4.1, as the Star Rail Fest presents a new twist.

A new Honkai: Star Rail Special Program has concluded, which means some fresh news about the game’s upcoming major update. Version 4.1, unveiled today as Unraveled for Daybreak, is the action RPG’s next moment, kicking off on March 25.

Unraveled for Daybreak is the next chapter in the ongoing story of Planarcadia, with the Astra Express Crew now invited to a fan fest inspired by their own past journeys. The aptly named Star Rail Fest is ostensibly hosted to allow more of the citizens of Arcadia to experience the Trailblaze.

As everyone’s eyes is fixated on the grand Star Rail Fest, the Phantasmoon Games continue to be in full swing, as does the war with the Supplicants. Star Rail Fest is, however, the big focus of this update, in case it wasn't obvious.

The event is made up of three large-scale zones, each themed around past excursions of the Astral Express. You’ll get to explore the Belobog Zone, Xianzhou Luofu Zone, and Penacony Zone. Later on, you’ll also be able to visit Pearluxe Tower, the headquarters of Pearluxe Corp.

Each area will feature its own attractions, such as the balloon figures of Supreme Guardian Cocolia and the Destruction Engine, the duel against the Lord Ravager Phantylia at Scalegorge Waterscape, and the Pearluxe Tower’s Alloy King Pom-Pom model.

The hot new arrival is bumbling noirish detective Ashveil whom we've met in Version 4.0, and who becomes a playable character with this update. Ashveil is a 5-Star Lightning-Type character, on the Path of The Hunt. You’ll be able to pull for him throughout 4.1's runtime, which is slightly reduced at four weeks instead of the usual six, in order to rebalance the schedule after the extra-long Version 3.8.

In combat, Ashveil is capable of increasing Crit Damage of all allies. He can also mark an enemy as Bait, which reduces the Defence of all enemies on the field so long as this tag holds. If Ashveil uses his Skill on the baited target, he will deal extra Damage and regain Skill Points for the team.

Ashveil can bully that baited target even further by launching Hounding Pursuit. If any of his teammates attacks the Bait, he can further deliver a follow-up attack that gradually accumulates Gluttony for as long as he’s in combat. Gluttony can later be consumed to boost follow-up attack damage.

If he lands a kill, Ashveil continues to deal damage to the next enemy he attacks. That buff is transferred if that enemy is killed. Even in map exploration, Ashveil can be deadly, capable of inflicting Stunned upon enemies within a specific range.

Returning characters this patch will be Hyacine in the first half, and Boothill in the second half. Once again, due to the reduced runtime, their banner reruns will be slightly shorter than normal, at just two weeks each instead of three — so be sure to take that into account if you're planning on pulling for either of them.

Version 4.1 also adds the Wispae War Saga, a new activity where you can practice your leadership skills by commanding different types of Wispae Soldiers in the Graphia Academy. You can upgrade each one, use spell cards to alter their effects, and later face other champions. You ultimately want to play this to unlock new Wispae Companions, not to mention complete the challenges within.

Finally, Version 4.1 marks the start of a new Arcadian Chronicles phase in the Divergent Universe. You’ll be able to use Waypoint Pass cards to explore the different areas. HoYo is also bringing back Planar Fissure and Garden of Plenty with double rewards. And as ever, if you log in for at least seven days after downloading the new patch, you’ll earn 10 premium banner pulls.

#4180. Feature: Box Art Brawl - Duel: Revenge Of The 'Gator

It's time for another edition of Box Art Brawl, can you believe it!

Last week, we took a look at two very different covers for NSO newbie Avenging Spirit on the Game Boy. The disparate designs did the North American variant no favours, as it wound up with only 30% of the vote, leaving the cuter Japanese and European cover to take the remaining 70%.

This time, we're turning to another newcomer in the Game Boy NSO library: Revenge of the 'Gator. This pinball game first arrived on the handheld back in 1989, and tasked players with tackling a series of paddle-based challenges across its main and bonus stages.

North America and Europe opted for the same design with this one, so it's another East vs West duel this week.

Review Pinball: Revenge of the 'Gator (3DS eShop / GB)

News Nintendo Expands Switch Online's Game Boy Library With Three More Titles

Update: Avenging Spirit, Mole Mania & Revenge of the 'Gator are now available

Well, there are some dynamics at play here, aren't there! These 'gators are not friendly. Look at those frowns! The angry ball return! The exploding scoreboard in the background! Honestly, we're pretty big fans of the composition here, with the giant ball and bumpers really selling the feeling of being inside a pinball machine.

This is a little bit friendlier. The 'gators have lost their frowns, the explosion is replaced by a rainbow, and instead of flicking the ball back to you, the friendly fella at the front is catching it. How sweet! Even the giant table itself has taken on a vibrant jungle theme.

Thank you for voting! We'll see you next week for another edition of Box Art Brawl!

Jim came to Nintendo Life in 2022 and, despite his insistence that The Minish Cap is the best Zelda game and his unwavering love for the Star Wars prequels (yes, really), he has continued to write news and features on the site ever since.

#4179. Here's The Best Graphics And Performance Mode For Phantom Blade Zero On PlayStation 5

Phantom Blade Zero is out now for everyone as a console exclusive on PlayStation 5 and on PC via Steam and the Epic Games Store as well. If you missed it, it's my favorite action game of the year so far, and you can read why in Game Informer's Phantom Blade Zero review. That explains why I think you should check the game out; Game Informer's list of Phantom Blade Zero tips and tricks will get you some key information I wish I had when I started the game; and this guide I wrote up about the requirements you need to get the best ending in Phantom Blade Zero will help you find all story-critical content in the game.

However, you're looking for advice on which of the three visual modes Phantom Blade Zero offers you should use on your PS5. This here piece is for you.

Phantom Blade Zero has three visual modes on PS5 Pro: Quality, Balanced, and Performance. I tested all three. My personal favorite was Balanced, which gives you an upscaled (checkerboarded) 4K resolution at 40 FPS, as long as you have a 120Hz TV with VRR. If you have a 120Hz TV, it likely has VRR because most major manufacturers include it with 120Hz. I like this mode because the upscaled 4K looks beautiful, just a hair less than native 4K, and if you aren't someone super trained on those details, I'd wager you won't notice the difference. The best part is that this mode offers 40 FPS gameplay, which, contrary to how math works, is halfway between 30 FPS and 60 FPS; I'm not kidding, look it up. As such, 40 FPS feels much smoother than 30 FPS, and you're still getting crisp 4K resolution. It's a win-win for me and my go-to mode when a game offers it. That said, if you don’t have a PS5 Pro, you won’t see this Balanced mode.

The Performance mode offers an upscaled 2K resolution with a pretty locked 60 FPS. Phantom Blade Zero is an extremely fast, fluid action game, so I think many people will want the buttery smoothness of 60 FPS gameplay. If that's you, pick the Performance mode. Sure, its resolution is lower, and it will look blurrier and less crisp than the other two modes, but if you aren't switching back and forth often or looking at side-by-side images, you likely won't notice.

Quality mode is native 4K resolution (absolutely beautiful, the best visual image you can get playing Phantom Blade Zero), but at 30 FPS... and for a game like this, I don't think 30 FPS does it justice. I don't really recommend this mode for combat, but if you're just waltzing around Wulin, grabbing screenshots and such, turn it on and bask in the wonders of developer S-Game's art team. Note: There is an option for ray tracing on PS5 Pro. I tested all three graphics modes with it on and off and noticed zero performance changes or issues. So, use ray tracing – it’s nice!

And, in case you missed it, below is an image of the PC system requirements and specs needed to play Phantom Blade Zero on Steam and the Epic Games Store:

In the meantime, read Game Informer's Phantom Blade Zero review, then check out our list of Phantom Blade Zero tips and tricks we wish we knew before starting the game. Then check out our breakdown of the requirements to see the best ending in the game.

#4178. Zenless Zone Zero Version 2.7 brings Angels of Delusion to the battlefield with playable Nangong Yu

Champions Never Fall to the Past indeed, as Zenless Zone Zero prepares for a major update that fans of Angels of Delusion will appreciate.

HoYoverse has delivered another Special Program for the second day running, this time for Zenless Zone Zero. The developer revealed the full details of Version 2.7, subtitled Champions Never Fall to the Past.

This next major update arrives March 24, adding two new Agents, and introducing the Hollow Champion competition.

Most things in Version 2.7 follow on from the Hollow Champion competition, which brings together old friends and familiar faces, as well interesting newcomers. Everyone is in it to win some big rewards and earn glory.

Among the unexpected participants the competition has attracted are the Public Security's Metropolitan Order Division, and even some former Calydon's Sweepers. A big challenge that awaits is Black Wolf Romeul, who’s capable of increasing his Crit Damage Resistance and Interruption Resistance by activating a Corruptive Barrier.

Romeul can also cause enemies to continuously lose HP, but you can beat him by putting together a squad that can deal sustained Anomaly damage, which will break through the barrier quickly.

Our first new arrival in Version 2.7 is Cissia of the Metropolitan Order Division. She is an S-Rank Electric Attack Agent who automatically gains three stacks of Venom when she enters the battle. Each stack deals Electric Damage while also increasing her Crit Rate for a time.

When she runs out of Venom, which will happen, Cissia can generate more stacks by using her EX Special Attack. She can also use her Basic Attack, Serpent's Kiss, to better utilise the new stacks of Venom she generates.

The other new Agent may be the more exciting. Nangong Yu, the captain and lead dancer of the Angels of Delusion, can now be part of your team. Nangong Yu is an S-Rank Ether Stun Agent who can boost her team’s Anomaly Buildup Rate against Stunned enemies.

Being part of an idol group has its perks, because she automatically regenerates Downbeat as time goes on, and even more any time a squad member inflicts an enemy with Anomaly. Nangong Yu can then use Downbeat - after enough has been accumulated - on charged attacks that keep enemies stunned for longer. Her Ultimate triggers Ether Veil: Delusion Reprise, which boosts the entire squad’s Attack.

Returning Agents in Version 2.7 will be Yidhari, the S-Rank Ice Rupture Agent, as well as Seed, the Electric Attack Agent.

Outside of all the very important action in the core story, this chapter also brings new themed events to Lumina Square’s Simmer Hot Pot Restaurant. The Simulated Battle Trial is also getting some love, with updated mechanics and new enemy line-ups.

Catch up on our recently updated Zenless Zone Zero character tier list, and don’t forget to check out these Zenless Zone Zero codes before you jump in for some free stuff.

#4177. Report: The Elder Scrolls 6 Gets Named Ahead Of Xbox Announcement, Plus Extra Details

It sounds like Xbox and Bethesda are getting set to announce the official name of The Elder Scrolls 6 in the coming weeks, as The Verge is reporting today that an announcement will be made at some point in November.

Spoilers ahead if you don't want to know the name!

According to the report, the name will be The Elder Scrolls VI: Sentinel, and Bethesda has been demoing gameplay of it to various people in recent months, including Xbox CEO Asha Sharma.

Sharma expressed how impressed she was with the game when she saw it in August:

The report also shares some extra details on what to expect in terms of The Elder Scrolls Vi: Sentinel's setting, claiming that it'll be set in Hammerfell and serve as "the first game about the history of the Elder Scrolls, and help uncover the secrets of these mysterious ancient artifacts".

Of course, Microsoft is probably getting set to reveal more about TES6 due to Xbox's 25th anniversary in November, but it might also be because Skyrim is turning 15 years old on November 11th, so perhaps that's the date to expect it.

In any case, we'll obviously bring you the official details if and when they're revealed next month!

#4176. Mass Effect 5 was aiming to offer a "level of autonomy and choice" that could vault it into orbit with Larian and CD Projekt's top RPGs, former dev says post-cancellation

"I'm sad you won't ever get to see what we were cooking"

Following EA's decision to shut down BioWare, the game that would've been the fifth entry in the Mass Effect series is being dumped out of an airlock, never to become a finished article that'll reach players hands as its creators envisioned. The larger tragedy is, of course, the job losses and the closure of a studio with a legacy befitting RPG royalty, but it's still sad that next Mass Effect will never come out, and some of the folks who worked on it have begun offering some insight into what the team were hoping to accomplish.

"I was one of the lucky ones who stayed with BioWare to start on the next Mass Effect, where I believe we were making something special: a level of autonomy and choice that no other game has been able to match," cinematic supervisor Tony de Waal wrote in a LinkedIn post revealing one of the 50 or so remaining BioWare staff let go as part of the closure. "We saw what Larian and CD Projekt were bringing to the table with their latest offerings, and started down a path to bring Mass Effect to the next level while remaining true to the Trilogy.

"I'm sad you won't ever get to see what we were cooking, and sad for the small, talented group of devs who were all punching above their weight to make something special. Please consider those who stayed with BioWare until the very end. They are truly some of the most talented people I've had the pleasure of working with throughout my career."

Writers Catherynne M. Valente and Derek Künsken didn't go into as much depth in their own posts on Twitter, but similarly echoed that they were excited about what the studio were sketching out and building with this Mass Effect game.

While it's worth maintaining the perspective that Mass Effect 5 was still early in development rather than minutes from being out of the door, it's galling that BioWare will never even get a chance to see if their plans could make for an RPG capable of pushing the genre forwards as the likes of Baldur's Gate 3, Cyberpunk 2077, and The Witcher 3 have over the past decade. Similarly to some of their long-established RPG-making cousins, the likes of Bethesda, BioWare's path hasn't been a straight line to massive success in recent years.

2017's Mass Effect: Andromeda wasn't as critically acclaimed and near-universally beloved as the trilogy that preceded it. Anthem failed to stick the live-service landing despite some promising ideas. Then, there was Dragon Age: The Veilguard, which had a well-documentedly messy development cycle that saw it pulled and pushed between multiplayer and singleplayer to suit the whims of EA management. The game it eventually turned into is one Nic (RPS in peace) summed up in his review as "a reluctant RPG, but a compelling, heartfelt action adventure". Sadly, it didn't sell the oodles of copies a game must to be deemed a success under EA these days, and thus seemed to instantly become the final black mark against BioWare that saw their corporate overlords start to fatally close in the walls.

Could BioWare have gotten their RPG master mojo back in full if they'd achieved their aims with Mass Effect 5? We'll never know. games studios under big publishers these days are rarely afforded such chances these days, no matter how obvious it might seem to those of us not just concerned with achieving short-term financial gains to offset being loaded up with debt in a Saudi-lead takeover by ditching everything that isn't turning over EA FC-level amounts of cash.

#4174. Heartopia goes to the movies with its next event

Heartopia's Whale Island will soon host a new event that's all about the magic of cinema.

Heartopia’s next in-game event has been announced, and it’s one you may not have seen coming. Developer XD Games revealed Dreamlight Cinematics Festival, an upcoming limited-time event that celebrates cinema and movie-making.

Dreamlight Cinematics kicks off March 21, and will run through May 1, available across the game’s PC and mobile versions.

Dreamlight Cinematics Festival takes place on Whale Island. And, perhaps as an unofficial Oscars tie-in, it’s all about classic Hollywood filmmaking. Not only that, it also celebrates the aesthetics and industrial design of that era.

All around the game’s world, you’ll be able to find festival-themed collectables, which you can then use to unlock free Time-Limited Exhibition Passes.

If you log in during the event’s runtime, you’ll get the Car Cinema furniture set for free. This cosmetic bundle comes with chairs that are modelled after vintage vehicles, as well as poster display stands with unique movie making-themed decorations.

If you’re looking to spend some money, the Deluxe Festival Pack comes with a large Island Sunset Billboard, which you can place outside your home so everyone knows you spent that money. The same pack also comes with the Popcorn Movie Ticket chat bubble skin, and a 10% bonus to Festival Tokens when you sell stuff at the store.

Regardless of which pack you get, you’ll earn collection points for each, which puts you on the path to unlocking outfits like the Dreamlight Cinematics Festival-specific Modern Show Dandy and Modern Show Belle. There’s also a Cinematic Moments building material set launching with this event.

For now, we have the above reveal trailer to go on, which does offer some idea of what it’s going to look like in-game. Until things kick off on the weekend, you best arm yourself with some Heartopia codes.

#4173. While EA shuts down BioWare, developers of The Sims, Skate, and Battlefield say they've also lost their jobs

Maxis and others appear hit by 400-strong layoff wave

Apparently the cliché "when it rains, it pours" also applies to corporate feculence. In addition to shutting down storied RPG makers BioWare, EA are reportedly cutting staff at The Sims developers Maxis, as well as Skate studio Full Circle and Battlefield 6 co-devs Ripple Effect.

EA's internal announcement - first made public by Bloomberg - allegedly declared that 400 staffers would be laid off. That greatly outnumbers the 50 or so that were working at BioWare, but the memo failed to specify which other studios would be affected. Vertical Slice have since reported that Maxis and Ripple Effect are among EA's targets, citing multiple LinkedIn posts by laid-off staff. Numerous Full Circle devs have also revealed their own redundancies.

Many of the affected are experienced staff who've been with their respective studios for years. Anna Huerta, Maxis' senior creative director for The Sims, shared that she was "impacted by today's restructuring," adding "I'm incredibly sad that I won't get to continue working alongside such talented people on projects we care so deeply about, but I'm looking forward to whatever comes next." Dylan Palmer, a Sims artist and art director who appears to have worked within EA since 2019, also posted that he was "unfortunately caught in the recent round of layoffs."

At Full Circle, who have already endured layoffs this year, John Epler - a seasonal creative director who'd previously spent 17 years at BioWare - confirmed the elimination of his role. As did senior designer David Milne, senior gameplay designer Jason Payne, software engineer Jessia Coan, and development director Megan Lengle. In a separate post, Epler also paid tribute to his former BioWare colleagues, writing: "I got to work with some incredibly talented people, and some incredibly talented teams. So to all of you who I crossed paths with over the years, whether we still talk regularly or haven't connected in a while, thank you. And I hope everyone's proud of what we did together."

Word of cuts at Ripple Effect, who've worked on Battlefield 6, Battlefield 2042, and the Battlefield Portal UGC platform, has also been corroborated by posts from character artist Corey Thomas, technical animator Juan Meza, and technical artist Turner Spring.

There's currently no suggestion that these studios, or their respective games, are being shuttered, cancelled, or otherwise treated like EA have treated BioWare and Mass Effect 5. Still, the money to pay off the billions of dollars in debt that the publisher took on, as part of its leveraged buyout by the the Public Investment Fund of execution enthusiasts Saudi Arabia, has to come from somewhere; EA have evidently decided that somewhere is their employees' livelihoods.

#4172. Feature: Nintendo Life eShop Selects (October 2026)

The best eShop games on Switch 1 & 2 in October

There have been a lot of them this month — too many to play, in fact. So if you're looking for the cream of the crop, and specifically the good video games on eShop that you can't (yet) buy in any physical form, you've come to the right place.

We've got six games this month that scored at least 7/10 in time for this showdown (and a couple more reviews in the oven which may qualify but aren't quite past the finish line at the time of writing).

As a reminder, these are Switch eShop games that don't have physical releases — which includes Game-Key Cards or codes-in-boxes — at the time of writing.

Our writers and contributors have voted for their top three eShop games of October 2026 and this is the result.

Before we get to the trio of podium places, let's see the other contenders:

Kicking off our top trio of appropriately spooky releases, we've got Wrong Organ's Mouthwashing. Coming to consoles a couple of years after its PC debut, we had heard great things — great and disturbing things — and we weren't disappointed.

"Simply put, Mouthwashing is a game best played when you’re lost in its grim setting, feeling like you, too, are stuck on the Tulpar and living this nightmare," wrote Rhiannon. "Its rich horror is found in every corner of the game and through every tool at the devs’ disposal. So it stands to reason that making it even easier to get lost in Mouthwashing — without sitting at your PC — only helps the game sink its teeth into you."

If you're looking for something great (and, indeed, disturbing) to play over Halloween, get this downloaded.

There's a Game-Key Card release coming, but not until next year. Therefore, RE4make REm4ke Resident Evil 4 Gold Edition takes its deserved second-place spot on the eShop Selects podium this month.

Ollie called it "the gold standard for modern remakes" in his review. "It updates the original beautifully, remaining faithful yet improving upon almost every element. The combat feels weighty and satisfying, the locations have all been expanded upon without feeling bloated, and there's enough content here to keep you coming back for years." If only we had that sort of time!

However, RE was held off the top spot this month by something similarly creepy though very different...

Spooky Doorway's The Séance of Blake Manor launched to critical acclaim on PC in 2025, and turned up on consoles exactly one year on, just in time for All Hallow's Eve. Again. And we were very glad to see it.

Especially Roland, who gave it a 9/10 and called it "something special" in his review, but it's evidently had the same effect on the rest of Team NL.

"Its broad cast of characters, vivid writing and engaging voice performances make it akin to curling up with an interactive, supernatural Agatha Christie novel – one that will spook you just enough for a cosy Halloween."

If you haven't tried this elsewhere, we urge you to give it a go now. Not even the lack of mouse controls puts a dint in it.

< Nintendo eShop Selects - September 2026

Do you agree with our ranking? Tell us about your favourite eShop releases of last month by voting in our poll and sharing your thoughts in the comments.

How we decide our eShop Selects top three: As we reach the end of every month, the Nintendo Life staff vote on their favourite titles from a list of games selected by the editorial team. To qualify for this list, these games must have been released as a digital-only Nintendo Switch eShop title in that particular month, and must have been reviewed on Nintendo Life; we select the qualifying games based on their review scores.

Staff are then asked to vote for three games that they think deserve to sit right at the very top of that list; first choice gets three points, second choice gets two points, and third choice gets one point. These votes are then tallied to create a top-three list, with the overall winner taking that month's top prize.

Gavin first wrote for Nintendo Life in 2018 before joining the site full-time the following year, rising through the ranks to become Editor. He can currently be found squashed beneath a Switch backlog the size of Normandy.

#4171. All the hype has already made Crimson Desert one of the biggest launches on Steam this year

We're merely days away from the end of the first quarter of 2026, and Crimson Desert has come in clutch to join the list of big sellers.

Crimson Desert, the open-world action RPG off-shoot from Korean MMO Black Desert Online, has officially launched, nearly six years after it was initially revealed. The game has been building up a lot of momentum over the years, which recently coalesced to turn it into one of 2026’s most anticipated titles.

All of it has been leading up to this moment, and the game appears to have landed smoothly, though not without controversy, as has seemingly become part of its MO.

It has not been 24 hours since Crimson Desert launched on PC and consoles, and it’s already become a big hit. On Steam, one of two stores where the game can be purchased (the other being the Epic Games Store), the game shot to the top of the charts.

The action RPG continued to accumulate more and more players on Steam, peaking at a very respectable 239,045 concurrent players (via SteamDB). Though its success was very much expected, we perhaps didn’t predict its peak would be that high.

Indeed, Crimson Desert has been in Steam’s top 100 global sellers list for six weeks, jumping up six spots to become the number one seller this week just before it launched. As we get closer to the weekend, the numbers could climb even higher.

This peak concurrent puts Crimson Desert in the same league as several of the other major releases of the first quarter of 2026. The top spot continues to belong to Slay the Spire 2, which peaked at a staggering 574,638 concurrent players. It happened just days after the juggernaut Resident Evil Requiem achieved its own 344,214 peak concurrent, which was the year’s highest up until Slay the Spire 2’s release. All three are well ahead of Nioh 3’s 88,045 peak concurrent, and Marathon’s nearly identical peak of 88,337.

Crimson Desert has seen something of a mixed reception by critics. James gave it three stars in our review, saying it “lacks the connective sinew to be truly functional,” which is a common criticism shared by other outlets. Many also lamented the sheer number of systems fighting for player attention, its poorly explained mechanics, and counterintuitive controls.

On Steam, at least, players have similarly been divided, with the current Steam user rating sitting at Mixed, based on 8,728 reviews. Unsurprisingly, most of the negative reactions fall on the clunky controls and the game’s tendency to, as one Steam user put it, “so miserably tries to be everything at once, and fails to be anything at all.”

#4170. The Duskbloods Delayed To 2027 So FromSoftware Can Adjust 'Game Rules And Balancing'

While the 2025 reveal of the Switch 2 came with many surprises, none were as unexpected as The Duskbloods. It's a Switch 2 exclusive, multiplayer-only title from FromSoftware, the developer behind games like Dark Souls and Elden Ring; in other words, not your typical Nintendo game. While The Duskbloods was originally scheduled to launch sometime this year, today the developer announced it's pushing the game's launch to 2027.

According to a post on The Duskbloods' X account, the main reason for the delay was balance-related. Here's the full statement:

While development of "The Duskbloods" is at the final adjustment stage, we have made the decision to move the launch window to 2027. We apologize to players who have been kindly awaiting the release of this title and thank you for your patience and support. During the network test, we saw active interest in the core concepts of the game, including combat, strategic depth, and player expression. To further enhance these aspects, we have decided to move the launch, allowing time for final adjustments to game rules and balancing.

We attended a hands-on preview session earlier this year and came away very positive, and sentiment was similar following the game's closed network test (that is, when the servers were working properly). It's not surprising that the devs have changes in mind following so much public feedback, though it is a little surprising that it will take until sometime next year for those adjustments to be complete.

To tide you over until the game's launch, check out our in-depth preview impressions or watch the video above to hear our live commentary over gameplay footage. You can also hear us discuss the game on our podcast, The Game Informer Show.

#4169. "We made a very difficult decision": Australian indie showcase Freeplay reject antisemitism claims after delisting a Jewish sponsor who was allegedly accused of being a "zionist"

Unnamed speaker criticised Unpacking dev's inclusion

The organisers of Australian independent games showcase Parallels have rejected accusations of "prejudice" and say they've received "violent threats", after a Jewish developer had her sponsorship of the event refunded. The developer in question is Wren Brier, creative director at Witch Beam. She claims an unnamed speaker booked for the event has accused her of being a "zionist", following an article about her work from an Australian Jewish publication.

On 8th October, Brier announced that Parallels organisers Freeplay had refunded and delisted her sponsorship, following complaints about her involvement from the anonymous speaker. According to Brier, the speaker called her a "zionist", apparently based on the presence of Witch Beam's 2021 puzzler Unpacking in a round-up of Israeli and Jewish-made videogames from The Jewish Independent, published on 5th October to mark this year's Melbourne International Games Week. Brier herself does not identify as Zionist and does not live in Israel, having left the country as a teenager.

There is much heated disagreement about what "Zionism" involves. Many protesters of Israel's vicious and inhuman war on Gaza define Zionism as a violent ethnonationalist project, comparable to European fascism, but the term has a long history that encompasses the desire for safety and security among Jewish people amid virulent antisemitism in other countries, before and after the Holocaust. I am not Jewish, and my understanding of these things is threadbare, but one thing we can say for sure is that being Jewish does not make you a Zionist. To conflate the two is actively antisemitic.

"I am Jewish," Brier wrote in her Bluesky thread from 8th October, which was posted a few hours before the Parallels event began. "I was born in Israel. I emigrated to Australia when I was 18. I did not serve in the military. I have never expressed any anti-Palestinian views. I really wanted to believe that 'zionist' wasn't a dogwhistle for 'Jewish' but I don't know what else it could be here.

"No one bothered to check whether the accusation was true," she went on. "The first I heard of any of this was this morning, when Freeplay told me they were refunding my donation and removing me as a sponsor because my mere name being listed 'has created an untenable environment' for their speakers."

Brier says she was not aware that Unpacking had been featured in the Jewish Independent piece. She credits the game's inclusion to the fact that it contains three Jewish cultural items - a dreidel, a menorah (pictured above on the table), and a hamsa, among hundreds of other objects the player is asked to unbox and arrange. "That was enough to make a speaker accuse me of being 'zionist', which in turn was enough for Freeplay to remove me as a sponsor, literally on the day of the event," Brier wrote.

"I've always loved Parallels, I've even participated in it myself and showed Unpacking there way back in 2018," she continued. "But I don't think I'll ever be able to support it or Freeplay again. I know at least one Freeplay board member has quit the board over this, too. This is discrimination, pure and simple."

Other game developers have come forward in Brier's support. "For the record, I had heard via-via murmurs of this and strongly objected to describing you as Zionist, and vouched for your person several times," wrote former Vlambeer co-founder Rami Ismail in response to her Bluesky thread. "I'm so sorry things played out like this. This is indeed deeply distressing."

Former Splash Damage writer Ed Stern added: "Wren, this is so stupid and absurd I don’t even know where to start."

Recently founded industry news site Vertical Slice have since obtained a copy of the email to Brier, informing her that her sponsorship had been refunded. "We value you as a member of the Freeplay community," it reads, "but unfortunately your involvement in Parallels has created an environment that is untenable for a number of our speakers, and it is very important to us that Parallels 2026 goes ahead. Freeplay has mixed feelings about this very difficult decision, and we sincerely wish our speakers had raised these concerns earlier so we could engage with you and look for a solution."

According to This Week In Videogames, meanwhile, two Freeplay board members in total have resigned over the decision to exclude Brier. TWIV further report that this year's Parallels event included several statements of support for Palestinians in Gaza, with addresses from Freeplay board member Joel Davidson and Origame Digital's Naphtali Faulkner, developer of the recent post-colonial horror Penguin Colony. Among the games featured at the event was Dreams on a Pillow, created by Palestinian developer Rasheed Abueideh, who was not present at the event, but recorded a video segment.

Supporters of Palestinians regularly call for a boycott of products made in Israel, and of projects or companies such as Microsoft that have business connections with the Israeli state and military. Unpacking does not appear to have any such links: according to Brier, it was made by developers based in Queensland, Australia, with funding from state body Screen Queensland. As for Brier's sponsorship of Parallels, she was not present at the event itself, but sent her studio logo for inclusion on the sponsor list.

Hitherto, Freeplay and Parallels have been affiliated with the Melbourne International Games Week, itself organised by the state cultural body the Australian Centre for the Moving Image. But according to a spokesperson, the ACMI "acted immediately to pause its support" after learning about Brier's delisting. “This was a clear breach of the Games Week code of conduct, which prohibits discrimination on any basis including sex, sexual orientation, gender, race, religion, disability, or any other protected attribute," the spokesperson told This Week In Videogames, noting that Freeplay are an independent entity and that they did not consult with the ACMI, before delisting Brier.

Now, finally, Freeplay themselves have come forward with a statement about the situation, which was sent to RPS among other outlets, following a request for comment yesterday. The statement doesn't identify the originator of the "zionism" claim.

"For 22 years, Freeplay has been a diverse, inclusive and welcoming place for people of many different backgrounds and perspectives to get together, chat about games and our lived experiences," it reads. "We can’t express how much we value our community, sponsors and donors and all of the support we have received over the years.

"Recently, the board decided to refund and remove acknowledgement of a donor from Parallels 2026," they go on. "The donor has been a valued member of the Freeplay community for many years. We regret the manner in which aspects of this process occurred and the upset this has caused within our community. We will be seeking further discussions with all affected parties to hopefully achieve a better outcome for the situation moving forward.

"The public discussion has included serious allegations about the motivations behind our actions," the statement acknowledges. "We reject suggestions that Freeplay acted out of prejudice towards any person or community. We made a very difficult decision under significant time pressure with the understanding that Parallels 2026 was at risk of not going ahead."

"We understand many of you would like clarity on the events from us," Freeplay write. "Given the sensitivities of the situation, and our responsibility to everyone involved, we won't be commenting on private communications or the various claims that have been made publicly. This week, members of our board have received violent threats, which we have reported to the police. We know that feelings in our community are running high. We ask that if you choose to engage online, please do so with care and respect for everyone involved."
